session_label: Patna public-source recovery and author-claim trace
scope: Desk-only follow-up after outreach was deferred. This pass rechecked public web, catalogue, bookstore, and archive surfaces for Patna Madrasa Sulaimania MS no. 2 / For Tomorrow no. 126, with no emails, library contact, interlibrary-loan requests, or scholar/publisher outreach.
questions_tested: Does any reachable public source identify Patna Madrasa Sulaimania MS no. 2 / For Tomorrow no. 126 as Jahanshah b. Qara Yusuf Haqiqi?
Can the earlier Bookvision author-identification claim be independently recovered?
Is the phrase 'Jahanshah b. Qara Yusuf Haqiqi Turkman' source-confirmed somewhere else in the public web corpus?
Does public metadata for the 2023 Patna catalogue expose entry-level text for manuscript no. 2?

executive_findings.finding: Reachable Patna evidence remains title-level only.
executive_findings.evidence_basis: The load-bearing Blogfa / Majma-i Zakhair-i Islami facsimile-series list gives Divan-i Haqiqi, manuscript no. 2, Madrasa Sulaimania/Sulaymaniyah, Patna, India; Persian / poetry; 126 pages; color. It does not give author heading, incipit, explicit, colophon, date, foliation, scribe, or first lines.
executive_findings.impact: Patna remains a high-priority unverified candidate lead outside data/witness_register.json.

executive_findings.finding: The 'Jahanshah b. Qara Yusuf Haqiqi Turkman' wording is confirmed on a separate printed-edition / bookstore lane, not on the reachable Patna source.
executive_findings.evidence_basis: IranKetab and search-result snippets from Iranian bookstore pages identify the author of a Behjat printed edition, Divan-i Jahanshah Haqiqi / Shah Turkman Shah Qaraqoyunlu, as Jahanshah b. Qara Yusuf Haqiqi Turkman. A related Jahanshahakyky blog post describes the Behjat / Khanegeldi Ownuk 1392/1393 printed book and says it is based on the Matenadaran manuscript.
executive_findings.impact: This likely explains the author phrase in external lead discussions, but it must not be retrofitted onto Patna MS no. 2 without entry-level Patna evidence.

executive_findings.finding: The 2023 Patna catalogue is still the decisive missing source.
executive_findings.evidence_basis: The Boroujerdi Telegram mirror states that the Patna catalogue introduces more than 200 manuscripts and contains bibliographic/codicological data plus images from some manuscripts. Public metadata and Alfehrest's public Telegram storefront confirm the catalogue identity and product metadata, but do not expose entry no. 2.
executive_findings.impact: The next non-outreach task is source recovery from public catalogue shadows, not register promotion.

executive_findings.finding: Bookvision remains unresolved from this environment.
executive_findings.evidence_basis: DNS resolution for www.bookvision.ir failed; direct fetch to https://www.bookvision.ir/Book.aspx?id=IGT236502 failed; web search for IGT236502 and Bookvision + Divan-i Haqiqi did not recover a cached record. India VPN retesting did not improve this: bookvision.ir A lookup timed out and www.bookvision.ir returned DNS server failure.
executive_findings.impact: Any Bookvision claim should remain marked as unrecovered until checked from a resolver/network that can reach bookvision.ir or from a preserved screenshot/cache.

executive_findings.finding: Torob confirms a live Alfehrest acquisition shadow for the facsimile title, but not entry-level Patna authorship evidence.
executive_findings.evidence_basis: Manual browser access and direct HTML retrieval through multiple regional routes exposed a live listing titled 'Divan-i Haqiqi (facsimile print)' sold by Alfehrest, with availability, seller, price, category, and image metadata.
executive_findings.impact: This materially strengthens the non-outreach acquisition path for the For Tomorrow / Patna facsimile, but it still does not identify the Patna manuscript's author as Jahanshah/Cihansah or expose incipit, explicit, colophon, foliation, date, scribe, or first lines.

executive_findings.finding: A Bing-indexed Alfehrest product result recovered the exact facsimile product slug and seller-page snippet.
executive_findings.evidence_basis: A Bing result for the exact query 'Divan-i Haqiqi' + 'Patna' returned the Alfehrest product URL https://alfehrest.com/product/%D8%AF%D9%8A%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%AD%D9%82%D9%8A%D9%82%DB%8C/ and a snippet naming 'Divan-i Haqiqi (facsimile print)', price 10,000,000 IRR, poetry / Persian, For Tomorrow no. 126, manuscript no. 2, Madrasa Sulaimania, Patna, India, color print, and add-to-cart wording.
executive_findings.impact: This independently ties the Torob facsimile to an Alfehrest product slug and confirms the same Patna/For Tomorrow metadata through a search-index cache. It still does not expose the full Alfehrest page, author heading, incipit, explicit, colophon, date, scribe, foliation, or first lines.

executive_findings.finding: Image-index and product-image recovery did not expose usable cover or OCR evidence.
executive_findings.evidence_basis: Bing Images queries for the exact facsimile title, Alfehrest title/slug, For Tomorrow no. 126, Patna, and Madrasa Sulaimania returned unrelated false positives. A manually accessed Torob page exposed the product image element and source URLs, but the image host requests timed out in the browser and the image element had naturalWidth/naturalHeight 0.
executive_findings.impact: No image/OCR evidence can currently supplement the text-index snippet. The remaining decisive evidence still requires the full Alfehrest page, the facsimile, or the Patna catalogue entry.

executive_findings.finding: Alfehrest's public Telegram storefront recovers the Patna catalogue product, not the manuscript entry.
executive_findings.evidence_basis: Telegram public search for the Alfehrest shop channel recovered posts 8982 and 9376. They identify the product as Fihrist-i nuskha-ha-yi khatti-i kitabkhana-yi Madrasa-yi Sulaymaniyah, Patna, Hindustan, give the Alfehrest product URL, author Tayebeh Hajj Baqerian, publisher Majma-i Zakhair-i Islami, price 3,200,000 IRR, and a cover image. A strict channel-wide pagination sweep of 619 public Telegram pages recovered no Divan-i Haqiqi facsimile product post; the only target-adjacent hits were the same Patna catalogue posts and keyword false positives.
executive_findings.impact: This strengthens catalogue acquisition metadata and clarifies that the Patna catalogue product is distinct from the For Tomorrow no. 126 facsimile. It still does not reveal the text of catalogue entry no. 2.

source_checks.observed: Post at lines 179-183 announces the Patna Madrasa Sulaimania catalogue launch at the 7 Ordibehesht 1402 / 27 April 2023 Qom conference; it says the catalogue covers more than 200 manuscripts, was prepared by Tayebeh Hajj Baqerian, contains bibliographic and codicological data plus images from some manuscripts, and was published in 100 copies by Majma-i Zakhair-i Islami with Oriental Company.

source_checks.source: Alfehrest public Telegram storefront search for Patna catalogue
source_checks.observed: The public Telegram view for Alfehrest shop channel @alfehrest2 returned posts 8982 and 9376. Post 8982, dated 2023-05-10, links to an Alfehrest product page titled 'Fihrist-i nuskha-ha-yi khatti-i kitabkhana-yi Madrasa-yi Sulaymaniyah, Patna Hindustan'. Post 9376, dated 2024-02-16, gives product metadata: product name 'Fihrist-i nuskha-ha-yi khatti-i kitabkhana-yi Madrasa-yi Sulaymaniyah, Patna Hindustan', price 3,200,000 IRR, subjects Iran print / Persian language / poetry / catalogue / manuscript cataloguing / recommended books / India / India studies, author Tayebeh Hajj Baqerian, publisher Majma-i Zakhair-i Islami, photographs by Sohail Asghar Thalethi, introduction by Seyed Sadeq Hosseini Eshkouri, and shortlink B2n.ir/t13221. The attached cover image reads 'Ganjineh-yi mirath-i makhtut (128)' and 'Fihrist-i nuskha-ha-yi khatti-i kitabkhana-yi Madrasa-yi Sulaymaniyah (Patna - Hindustan)'.
source_checks.interpretation: Strong seller-side acquisition metadata for the Patna catalogue, but not manuscript-entry evidence. It also separates the catalogue product and cover series number from the For Tomorrow no. 126 facsimile listing.

source_checks.source: Alfehrest public Telegram storefront facsimile-title sweep

A strict channel-wide pagination sweep scanned 619 public Telegram pages with zero fetch errors. The sweep surfaced 9 target-adjacent keyword hits: Khanqah Mujibiyah Patna catalogue post 2290, unrelated Istanbul Sulaimania/Suleymaniye catalogue posts 2317, 2404, and 7014, unrelated Divan-i Azar Khorasani posts 7838 and 12248, unrelated 'For Tomorrow 5' post 7924, and the already-known Patna catalogue posts 8982 and 9376. None exposed the For Tomorrow no. 126 Divan-i Haqiqi facsimile, Patna manuscript no. 2 entry text, author heading, incipit, explicit, colophon, date, scribe, foliation, or first lines.

source_checks.source: Torob product page for Divan-i Haqiqi (facsimile print)
source_checks.access_result: reachable through manual browser access and later retrievable as HTML through multiple regional routes
source_checks.observed: The page title was 'Buy and price Divan-i Haqiqi (facsimile print) | Torob'. Embedded product data identified the item as 'Divan-i Haqiqi (facsimile print)', with price, seller, availability, category, product image URL, and seller profile domain alfehrest.com. Regional direct HTML fetches returned HTTP 200 and schema.org Product data with matching seller and availability fields. Attempts to resolve the outbound seller link did not return a stable Alfehrest product page, so the stable recovered evidence is the Torob HTML and embedded product data rather than a resolved Alfehrest page.
source_checks.interpretation: Strong live acquisition and availability evidence for the facsimile title; not sufficient to classify Patna MS no. 2 as a Jahanshah/Cihansah witness.

source_checks.source: Bing Images and Torob product-image recovery
source_checks.access_result: image index reachable; target images unrecovered
source_checks.observed: Bing Images was queried for the exact title 'Divan-i Haqiqi (facsimile print)', title plus Alfehrest, site:alfehrest.com/product plus title, both hyphenated slug forms, the 10,000,000 price string, Patna, For Tomorrow no. 126, and Madrasa Sulaimania. Result sets contained unrelated false positives rather than Alfehrest/Torob product-card images. The manually accessed Torob page exposed product image src https://image.torob.com/base/images/eF/to/eFto-XkFI9Z6zdst.jpg_/280x280.jpg and currentSrc https://image.torob.com/base/images/eF/to/eFto-XkFI9Z6zdst.jpg_/560x560.webp, but the element reported naturalWidth 0 and naturalHeight 0. Playwright network logs showed repeated image.torob.com requests for the 560x560 and 300x300 product images failing with net::ERR_TIMED_OUT.
source_checks.interpretation: Image/OCR mining did not add evidence beyond the Bing text snippet. The Torob product image URL is known but not recoverable from this route.

source_checks.observed: Direct Alfehrest search and guessed product-slug routes for Divan-i Haqiqi timed out in both shell and Playwright, even though Torob's seller page identified alfehrest.com as the seller domain. UAE, Turkey, and India VPN retests resolved alfehrest.com to 195.28.169.45 and TCP ports 80/443 succeeded, but HTTPS timed out before completing TLS and HTTP accepted a GET request then returned zero bytes before timeout. Home, search, guessed Divan-i Haqiqi product routes, WordPress REST endpoints, sitemap.xml, product-sitemap.xml, post-sitemap.xml, product category sitemap, RSS feed, B2n shortlink t13221, and the known Alfehrest Patna-catalogue product URL all failed without usable response content from this machine. After Bing recovered the exact product slug /product/%D8%AF%D9%8A%D9%88%D8%A7%D9%86-%D8%AD%D9%82%D9%8A%D9%82%DB%8C/, direct curl and Jina Reader attempts against that slug and the www variant also timed out.
source_checks.interpretation: Alfehrest remains a decisive acquisition surface, but its own HTTP application responses were not recovered in this pass. UAE, Turkey, and India are sufficient for Torob HTML and Telegram public storefront search, but not sufficient for an Alfehrest HTTP response from this machine.

inference: The strongest current hypothesis is that the Patna source trail and the Behjat/Ownuk printed-edition source trail have been partially conflated in external discussion. The title Divan-i Haqiqi at Patna is real enough to prioritize, and Torob plus Bing now confirm a live Alfehrest acquisition route and exact product slug for a facsimile-print product under that title. However, the author formula Jahanshah b. Qara Yusuf Haqiqi Turkman is currently documented on separate printed-edition/bookstore surfaces, not on directly read Patna evidence. Public text-searchable Alfehrest Telegram mining supports the catalogue acquisition path but did not recover the facsimile product or manuscript-entry evidence, and image/OCR routes did not recover usable product-card or cover evidence. Until the Patna catalogue entry or facsimile is inspected, the Patna item should remain an unverified title-level lead.
